senses.definition: (UK dialectal, Northern England, Scotland) To desist, to stop, to cease.
examples: Till all war deaun I knaw thou wad not lin.

quotes.text: Halfe furious vnto his foe he came, / Resolv'd in minde all suddenly to win, / Or soone to lose, before he once would lin [...].
quotes.reference: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book I, Canto I”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London: […] [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:

quotes.text: He never linned till he had taen away every chicken that the wife had.
quotes.reference: 1822, The Three Perils of Man, James Hogg, I. 238:

examples: Here the hammer's active din / Blends with sound of roaring lin.
Whan they came to the roaring lin, She drave unwitting Isabel in.
A step farther might be on the firm earth; but more probably it would be illusive, and dash him into the roaring Lin, where he would be ingulfed at once in its furious whirlpool.

O ye were ne ' er the ane to fret,
But kept my heart aboon,
Wi ' smiles sweet as when first we met,

quotes.text: And therefore, to recount her Rivers, from their Lins (marginal gloss) Meeres or Pooles, from whence Rivers spring
What seek we here / Amid this waste where desolation scowls, / And the red torrent, brawling down the linn, / Sings everlasting discord?

senses.definition: (Scotland, Ireland, Northern England, especially in compounds) Alternative form of line (“flax, linen”).
examples: a lin apron, lin-break, lin-brake, a lin cap, lin-clout, lin-garn/lin-yarn, lin-man, lin-weaver/lin-webster, lin-wheel
Paddeys wi' their feyne lin' ware.
Hoo wur stonnin' i' th' front of a weshin'-mug, wi' a lin brat afore her.
